no_overhang.meaning: flat book does not overhang: edge pinch fails until Expose

crowded.meaning: both pinch axes of the block have a finger slot taken (3 mm gaps)

not_in_view.meaning: the target object is out of the first view (another surface or room)

start_elsewhere.meaning: the robot starts elsewhere, facing away from the task area

tool_away_from_surface.meaning: the tool is on another surface than the one to work on

small_container_present.meaning: a too-small container is in view; the large one must be chosen

no_cup.meaning: the requested object does not exist; the allowed substitute is used

no_pen.meaning: the requested object does not exist; the allowed substitute is used

destination_occupied.meaning: the first destination has no free spot; the other allowed one is used

microwave_broken.meaning: the microwave runs but does not heat: the stove

lid_on.meaning: collect is refused while the lid is on: Uncover first

container_absent.meaning: the named container is absent; the stated substitute is used

surface_cluttered.meaning: objects stand where the work happens (the wiped strip): move them aside, do the work, put them back

cookware_choice.meaning: several vessels by the food, only one supports every step (stirring, lid, burner): choose it over the nearer ones

appliance_occupied.meaning: the usual appliance is taken by something else; another one does the job without clearing it (clearing stays allowed)

spot_quality.meaning: the destination has free spots that violate the instruction (crowding the place settings, hidden, at the edge): choose the spot from what is observed

unstable_base.meaning: the obvious base lies at the edge: stack on the other one or move it in first

joint_capacity.meaning: several containers, only one holds every item together: allocate the items jointly

anchor_boxed_in.meaning: the object to set things next to has no room around it: move it to where the whole setting fits

destination_full.meaning: the destination has no room left: move what occupies it to a legal place, then put the object there

item_out_of_view.meaning: one of several items to collect is in another room, out of view: search, then route the collection

decoy_destination.meaning: a container that the instruction does not allow stands where the named one should be

state_differs.meaning: the world is already in a different state than the usual plan expects

workspace_choice.meaning: the action cannot be done where the object is (no room to turn the book over inside the shelf): move it to a place where it can, then back

history_exclusion.meaning: the usual choice is ruled out by what happened before (the kid found the block in the pot last time): pick another one that meets the goal

count_against_need.meaning: count what is there against what is needed and act on the difference only (nothing, or fetch the missing ones)

agent_ability.meaning: where or what follows from what another person can do (the kid reaches only low shelves), even against where the thing usually belongs

goal_by_example.meaning: what to do is shown by an example in the scene (a set place): copy which things and where, in the frame of the person it is for; a missing kind is replaced by the closest one in the same spot

rule_induction.meaning: several examples follow rules that depend on who they are for (adults: a mug, the kid: a plastic cup); induce the rules and apply the one that fits

relational_exception.meaning: objects of one kind are treated differently by how they stand: the blocks built into the kid's castle stay, loose ones are put away

preference_allocation.meaning: one of the items is set aside for a person; which one follows from what the instruction says about them (the kid does not like oranges)

subgoal_order.meaning: the subgoals must be ordered so each step is feasible (the empty tray to its place first, then the fruit onto it; never lift a loaded tray)

closed_fridge.meaning: the item is in the closed fridge next to the work spot: open it, take the item, close it again (the Action-Level part of a Task-Level design)

disposal_by_state.meaning: the instruction names kinds of destination (trash, fridge, counter); which object goes where follows from what it is and its state (an empty disposable tray is rubbish, a glass box with food is leftovers)

resource_in_use.meaning: the resource the instruction names is there but already in use (a pot full of other soup): it is not to be used or disturbed; another one is fetched

category_rule.meaning: the instruction gives a rule by kind (the kid's toys away, the kitchen things stay); what happens to each object follows from what it is

storage_place.meaning: the item is to go back where it is normally kept; that place is not named and follows from the scene (where items of its kind are kept)

referent_clue.meaning: the instruction names the object or place by a clue (whose it is, where it was used), not by its name; the nearest look-alike is not the one meant

infeasible_fallback.meaning: under the stated constraints the goal may not be reachable: check, and if not, take the fallback the instruction names instead of breaking a constraint

appliance_compatibility.meaning: which appliance can heat an item follows from its container (metal not in the microwave, a ceramic bowl not on the burner)

arrangement.meaning: several objects make one layout (a row, spacing, squared): each placement leaves room for the next

viewer_place.meaning: the instruction names who is to see it, not where: the place follows from where the viewer is

goal_already_met.meaning: what the instruction asks for already holds: check, and do not fetch again

unknown_count.meaning: how many items the goal covers is not said: search every place before stopping

goal_items_unstated.meaning: the instruction names a purpose; which items it needs is to be inferred

count_from_scene.meaning: how many items to bring is read off the scene, not the instruction

errands_combined.meaning: two errands meet at one place; an order that joins them saves a trip

missing_piece.meaning: the goal needs one more piece than the house has (no third block); another item of the kind the instruction names (another toy) stands in, in another room; a look-alike of another kind nearby (the sponge) does not count

destination_unnamed.meaning: several places fit the instruction's words; which one is meant (the table the guests eat at) shows only on looking, possibly in another room

item_put_away.meaning: the item is in one of several closed places the instruction names

multi_object_goal.meaning: the goal has several ordered or allocated subgoals

resource_absent.meaning: the usual thing is not in the house; the closest thing that serves the purpose is used (a sponge for tissues, a mug for a soup bowl)

dependent_decisions.meaning: two or three decisions in a row, each on what the step before found (the usual thing is absent -> a substitute -> the substitute is put away)
